page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable cloud instance based on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The hardware configuration features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. The processor carries 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache pool, alongside vector and matrix extension instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. Memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, providing a standard balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not bundle any local NVMe or SSD storage and includes zero integrated GPUs. Networking throughput is defined at a baseline of 15 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-tier execution in static web serving throughput (105.74 GB/sec), Geekbench image processing (20,897.0), and 70B parameter model prompt processing (39.14 tokens/sec). Multi-core processing capabilities are robust, showing strong results in the Geekbench multi-core suite (20,583.0), stress-ng multi-threaded runs (69,359.48), PassMark database operations (29,579.98), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (440.95 GB/sec).

Because the m8i-flex series utilizes burstable CPU allocation, resource access is optimized for variable workloads rather than sustained maximum compute saturation. Its memory configuration yields strong read bandwidth (197.6 GB/sec large block uncached, 5,112.66 GB/sec small block cached), though write operations settle into average performance tiers (79.1 GB/sec large block). The combination of high core counts, DDR5 bandwidth, and AMX hardware acceleration delivers efficient price-performance for high-throughput web serving, build farms, intermediate caching systems, database operations, and CPU-driven quantized machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 32 physical cores, 64 burstable vCPUs, and 480 MB of L3 cache. It provides 256.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, with a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated graphics processing units. In performance testing, it exhibits top-tier static web serving throughput (105.74 GB/sec) and prompt processing efficiency for large language models, supported by AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Benchmark results also indicate strong multi-core computation, compilation throughput, and database transaction capacity. Given its burstable execution profile and absence of local disks, m8i-flex.16xlarge is technically aligned with scalable web application backends, containerized microservices, distributed caching, and CPU-based inference workloads.
